subject: Pilot intake: parallelism & capacity - post-call action items
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@finledger.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Pilot intake: parallelism & capacity - post-call action items

Alex — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment heading into the pilot: 

Recap (from today)
- Primary goal: validate a low-latency, high-throughput inference path for FinLedger’s real-time reconciliation feature.
- Target traffic profile discussed: sustained ~400–500 QPS of short text generation requests (avg prompt+response ~120 tokens), with brief bursts up to ~1,200 QPS.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency target <= 120 ms end-to-end; p99 ideally < 250 ms.
- Concurrency / connections: estimated 180–250 concurrent logical sessions (these map to independent user sessions that may multiplex over connections).
- Streaming: client uses chunked streaming; we need a stable per-connection multiplexing strategy plus a prefix cache for common prompt templates.

Open items we promised to follow up on
1) Redwood quota/rate-limit proposal that supports the above traffic profile (connection pool sizing, per-connection QPS, burst window + credits).
2) Concrete pilot configuration (duration, dedicated pool vs shared, telemetry hooks we will expose).
3) Pricing / pilot credits and any contract milestones (procurement timeline you mentioned).

Attachments: I’m attaching a short proposal and an SLO metrics worksheet (redwood-conn-proposal.pdf, slo-metrics.xlsx).

Immediate next steps
- Internal: Aditya/Dev — can you review capacity proposal and reply with a recommended quota profile by tomorrow EOD?
- Alex/Priya — can you confirm the expected peak concurrency (180–250 range) and whether you need guaranteed burst capacity during month-end reconciliation windows?
- Kimberly/Marissa — I’ll draft a pilot term summary and send a DocuSign link once we lock quotas.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0143

From: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@finledger.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finledger.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot intake: parallelism & capacity - post-call action items

Kimberly — thanks for the succinct recap and for the materials. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Concurrency: 200 concurrent logical sessions is the median target; on month-end runs that could spike to ~350 for 15–30 minutes. That spike behavior is our main concern.
2) Burst behavior: those spikes are short (<= 45s) but very high QPS; we need a clear burst credit/overage policy so our app doesn’t fail.
3) Streaming: we intentionally use streaming to present partial reconciliation results to the user; stable chunk latencies are more important than absolute final latency for some flows.
4) Procurement: procurement has asked for a pilot agreement and pricing for evaluation (they want to see a 30-day pilot + an option to convert to a 12-mo committed plan). Any chance you can include a nominal pilot credit?

Questions for Redwood team:
- Can you confirm a recommended per-connection QPS limit and whether you support multiplexing (multiple logical sessions per TCP connection)?
- How does Redwood handle short, high spikes in QPS (burst windows and temporary overcommit)?
- What observability will be available in the pilot (token-level cost, per-route p95/p99, trace IDs)?

If you can respond to the three bullets above we’ll route to procurement. Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Reynolds
Head of Product
FinLedger
alex.reynolds@finledger.com | +1 650-555-0122

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@finledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot intake: parallelism & capacity - post-call action items

Alex / team — quick technical answers and a recommended quota profile. Posting the core items here so procurement and engineering have the same reference.

Answers:
- Multiplexing: yes — Redwood supports HTTP/1.1 keep-alive + HTTP/2 multiplexing for streaming. Recommended: start with up to 4 logical sessions per connection for the pilot (reduces socket pressure while giving per-session isolation).
- Per-connection QPS: we recommend a conservative baseline of 10 requests/s per connection for streams with small payloads; with multiplexing that maps to ~40 logical requests/s per socket.
- Burst handling: we recommend a burst window model: baseline quota = 400 QPS sustained, burst capacity = 1,200 QPS for 60s with an enforced cool-down and soft throttling after 60s. We can expose burst credits (30s of additional burst capacity) for month-end windows by schedule.
- Concurrency mapping: based on your numbers, set the logical-session concurrency target = 250; reserve 300 sockets for the pilot pool to support multiplexing and headroom for retries.

Proposed pilot quota (recommended) — attach this to the pilot agreement:
- Baseline QPS: 400 sustained
- Burst QPS: 1,200 for up to 60s (soft-throttle thereafter)
- Scheduled burst credits: additional 30s burst allowance for two scheduled month-end windows during pilot
- Connection pool: 300 sockets (supports ~1,200 logical sessions at 4x multiplexing)
- Max simultaneous streams per socket: 4
- Token-level telemetry: p50/p95/p99 by route, per-request tokens, and KV cache hit rates (we’ll provide Grafana + access to the telemetry export).

Attachments: I’ve attached a short SLO worksheet with how these quotas map to observed latencies (slo-metrics.xlsx).

Caveats / operational notes:
- If you see sustained error rates with soft throttling we’ll engage dedicated capacity for the pilot (we can turn on a reserved pool for a short period).
- Billing: pilot usage will be recorded separately; we can provide a one-time credit to cover early pilot overages (Kimberly — I left the amount blank for commercial to propose).

Happy to discuss these numbers on a short tech sync if helpful.

— Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@finledger.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot intake: parallelism & capacity - post-call action items

Alex / Priya — thanks for the details and for confirming the month-end spike behavior. Proposal / next steps below: 

Commercial pilot proposal (summary)
- Duration: 30 days from start date.
- Pilot environment: dedicated pilot pool (reserve a small dedicated cluster) to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
- Quotas: follow the recommended pilot quota from Aditya (Baseline 400 QPS / Burst 1,200 QPS / 300 sockets / 4x multiplexing).
- Pilot credit: Redwood will provide a $10k pilot credit to offset overages during evaluation; any additional committed capacity will convert to a paid contract.
- Observability: access to a Grafana dashboard with p50/p95/p99, per-route token counts, KV cache hit rates, and request-level trace IDs.

Operational plan and decision points
- FinLedger to confirm: exact dates for the two month-end windows we should pre-schedule for burst credits; expected spike durations.
- Procurement: Kimberly will send a short pilot agreement (DocuSign) with the quotas above once Alex confirms dates.
- Tech handoff: schedule a 30–45 min tech-check with Aditya and Dev to finalize connection pool and multiplexing settings ahead of cutover.

If that looks good I’ll get a DocuSign out today and a short runbook for the pilot cutover. Appreciate the fast responses — looking forward to getting this running.

Thanks — Kim

--

Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
